Issued at 1223 PM CST Sun Nov 8 2026

This week into early next weekend ...

Rest of Today: GOES East water vapor imagery indicates the cold 
core upper low over the northeast US continues to slip
northeastward into eastern Canada while an additional upper low 
remains near the Sierra Madres area of western Mexico. 

High cirrus are continuing to spreading across the region this
afternoon while at the surface a 1024-1025mb surface high builds
in which has resulted in light winds across the area. Temperatures
are warming into the upper 60s northwest of the Natchez Trace of 
Interstate 20 while upper 60s to low 70s to the southeast with
lows tonight seasonably cool, generally n the mid 30s F to lower
40s F. Patchy frost is possible again tonight as conditions will 
likely be similar to those seen last night-- winds near calm with 
effective radiational cooling. There remains potential for cirrus 
cloud decks to stubbornly stick around into tonight downstream of 
the SW US upper low, which could keep temperatures from dropping 
as much as they would in clear sky conditions. Frost was observed 
in some locations this morning and with little airmass change, 
additional pockets of frost are likely tonight, particularly in 
areas that are sheltered/low-lying and see somewhat thinner cirrus
canopy. Limited HWO graphic for patchy frost remains for tonight,
mainly in north-central and east to northeast MS. Ensure plants 
are covered or indoors and take consideration of cold temperatures
and impacts to pets and people.

This Week Into Next Weekend: Quiet, cloudy and mostly dry pattern
will persist this work week. Moist, isentropic ascent and cloudy 
conditions will remain draped across the Gulf Coast states through
at least mid-week (Wednesday). The upper low ejecting out from the
Southwest is still projected to become an open shortwave and the
primary noticeable affects with that feature will be mostly
changes in cloud cover. Wedged between the east coast trough and
the weakening incoming southern stream shortwave, upper heights
early week will actually see some slight rises and highs will 
moderate to seasonable through mid week (70 F to 78 F Monday to 
74 F to 80 F by Wednesday). Lows will remain seasonable.

Following this shortwave, guidance has come into agreement that a
northern stream shortwave, more potent than the previous, will
follow quickly on its heels. This will push a reinforcing cold
front into the area with perhaps a few sprinkles or isolated 
showers. The best chance for any accumulation will be north of 
I-20 where generally less than 0.05" could be possible. Most areas
stay dry. This reinforcing shortwave will serve to deepen the 
eastern CONUS troughing overall and a drier and cooler pattern 
into late week is expected. 

Friday and likely again on Saturday, additional spokes of
vorticity/shortwaves rotate our way down the westward side of the
long wave trough which further deepens the upper troughing and
reinforces the suppressed, cool and dry weather. In fact, the
pattern becomes so amplified that at 500 mb, guidance generally 
agrees it will be colder over portions of our area than in 
portions of far northern Canada with heights at that level sinking
to 35 dam below climatological average.

Fortunately, it's still "merely" approaching mid November and 
these anomalies won't likely bring bone-chilling cold. However, it
is looking more likely that many areas (particularly near and 
north of I-20) could see their first light freeze by Saturday or 
Sunday morning with widespread frost possible. Blended guidance as
of this morning suggest probabilities of a light freeze are a 
medium to high chance (40 to 70 percent) for central east and 
north- northeast MS, while falling at 30 degrees or below are low 
to medium chance (20 to 50 percent). Early guidance this afternoon
supports this general idea. HWO graphics for frost/freeze are 
beginning to look more likely with potential for heightened 
messaging. The exact depth and orientation of the cold airmass 
introduces uncertainty--our area will be on the western edge of 
the coldest airmass meaning small shifts east or west could mean 
multiple degrees of difference in temperature. For that reason, 
will continue to monitor trends without formally issuing HWO 
products at this time. /DC/86/
